nodes.label: AES-256-GCM API Key Encryption
nodes.rationale: Tenant API keys are stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext. TENANT_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is a 32-byte key, base64 or 64-character hex. Ciphertext from scripts/encrypt-api-key.mjs uses a v1: prefix. The key is decrypted only in memory for the GoHighLevel call. The upsert script reads the private-integration token from stdin so it is not a process argument.

nodes.label: Tenant Timezone Calendar Dates
nodes.rationale: src/time/business-date.ts supplies tenant-timezone calendar dates. timezone is an IANA name used for calendar-day math and defaults to UTC. Interval collapse, order-date writes, M10 lock dates, the full-reconcile weekday, and days since last order all use that calendar. A Chicago location is still on Thursday at 03:00 UTC Friday, so its Friday full scan runs on the Saturday 03:00 UTC hop.

nodes.label: Cron Bearer Secret
nodes.rationale: The dispatcher rejects the call unless CRON_SECRET is set and the Authorization bearer token matches. Each per-tenant POST is invoked with that same bearer token, and the tenant route repeats the check.

nodes.label: API Key Encrypt Script
nodes.rationale: scripts/encrypt-api-key.mjs encrypts a token from stdin without writing a database row, for TENANT_STORE=env. Output is v1: ciphertext using TENANT_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Stdin is used so the token is not an argument.

nodes.label: Environment Tenant Store
nodes.rationale: One tenant, either as TENANT_CONFIG JSON or as discrete TENANT_* variables. When TENANT_CONFIG is set, the discrete fields are ignored. apiKey and apiKeyEncrypted are mutually exclusive. A plaintext apiKey is encrypted with TENANT_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY before the rest of the service sees it. Do not set TENANT_API_KEY together with TENANT_API_KEY_ENCRYPTED. upsert changes the process copy only. webhookTokenHash is also accepted inside TENANT_CONFIG and is required in every environment, including Preview. TENANT_NAME defaults to the location id. TENANT_TIMEZONE defaults to UTC. TENANT_CURRENCY defaults to USD and is stored only; amounts are not rescaled.

nodes.label: Field Catalog Generator
nodes.rationale: npm run generate:fields regenerates src/schema/fields.ts after a fixture change. That catalog is keyed for runtime lookup, but the embedded ids are the RX Test Lab reference only.

nodes.label: GoHighLevel HTTP Client
nodes.rationale: Timeout, retry with exponential backoff and jitter on HTTP 429, HTTP 5xx, and network failures, capped at 20 seconds. Retry-After is honored up to 60 seconds. Per-location spacing defaults to 100ms between requests on a warm instance and is process-local. Orders use GET /payments/orders with locationId, altId, altType=location, optional contactId, limit=100, and offset until totalCount. The client does not issue one limit=500 request and does not send startAt or endAt. A page cap throws instead of writing metrics from a partial history. Orders for a different contactId are dropped. The daily reconcile uses the same path without contactId and reads one page at a time. Detail uses GET /payments/orders/{orderId} with the same spacing and timeout. Contact search is POST /contacts/search with pageLimit and searchAfter. Contact updates are PUT /contacts/{contactId} with id, key, and field_value. Workflow enrollment POST is not retried. altId and altType=location are sent on every order request. The default order list is newest-first by createdAt.

nodes.label: GoHighLevel
nodes.rationale: External CRM. A standard Webhook action posts the contact's fields at the top level (contact_id, location.id, name, email, phone) and the action's Custom Data under customData, and cannot set headers. Default API base is https://services.leadconnectorhq.com with version header 2021-07-28.

nodes.label: Idempotency Store
nodes.rationale: SET NX with TTL. Upstash Redis via KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN, or the UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_* pair only when the KV pair is unset. A URL from one pair and a token from the other are ignored. Production fails closed when the KV pair is missing. Other environments use memory when neither pair is set. Keys: evt:{locationId}:{contactId}:{eventId} (300s, only for eventId or webhookId); lock:{locationId}:{contactId} (30s); rerun:{locationId}:{contactId} (120s); m10:{locationId}:{YYYY-MM-DD} (at least 360s, released when the hop finishes); m10cursor (2 hours); m06reconcile and m06full (36 hours when finished, 2 hours while a cursor is in progress, at most 2000 contact ids); m10enroll:{locationId}:{contactId} (180 days, deleted when not eligible). YYYY-MM-DD is the tenant timezone date. The Vercel Marketplace KV_URL, REDIS_URL, and KV_REST_API_READ_ONLY_TOKEN are not read.

nodes.label: Local Checks
nodes.rationale: npm install, npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run lint. Node.js 22.18 or newer. Tests use mocked fetch, in-memory stores, and the test-lab fixture. They do not call GoHighLevel, Neon, or Upstash, so the suite does not need live credentials.

nodes.label: Daily M06 Order Reconcile
nodes.rationale: The test-lab account only has an Order Submitted workflow trigger, so a cancel, refund, or payment-status change on an existing order never calls the webhook. Before win-back eligibility, the tenant hop lists GET /payments/orders with altType=location and altId and no contactId, and collects distinct contacts whose updatedAt, or createdAt when updatedAt is missing, falls inside M06_RECONCILE_HOURS (default 48; invalid values use 48). The list is newest-first by createdAt, not updatedAt. startAt and endAt filter createdAt by whole days in the location timezone (the end day is inclusive and an ISO time is rounded to a day), so they cannot see a recent update on an older order and the scan does not send them. It pages with offset and limit=100 and stops after M06_RECONCILE_MAX_PAGES (default 30, about 3000 of the most recently created orders; invalid values use 30). Hitting that cap logs a warning with the location id, pages scanned, and createdAt of the last order, and eligibility still runs for contacts already refreshed. An older update is caught by the weekly full reconcile or by the contact's next nudge, which only happens when they place a new order. If the hop's time budget runs out during the scan, it stores m06reconcile:{locationId}:{YYYY-MM-DD} with the next offset and the contact ids already handled, and waitUntil resumes the scan. A finished scan is remembered for 36 hours so a later pass the same local day does not list orders again. Each contact runs the same recompute as the webhook: the per-contact lock, the metrics hash write-skip, and the per-location rate limiter. Order payloads are not logged. The reconcile is what writes M06 fields.

nodes.label: M06 Field Contract
nodes.rationale: M06 writes total_orders, qualifying_order_count, first_order_date, last_order_date, lifetime_value, average_order_value, highest_order_value, lowest_order_value, customer_type, customer_status, lifecycle_stage, last_order_location, last_order_type, average_order_interval_days, typical_order_interval_days, orders_last_30_days, orders_previous_30_days, spend_last_30_days, spend_previous_30_days, order_frequency_trend, spending_trend, days_since_last_order, expected_next_order_date, days_overdue, overdue_ratio, favorite_item, top_items, preferred_order_type, preferred_location, purchase_consistency, order_source_mix, primary_order_source, metrics_hash, and m06_intelligence_updated_at. It never writes winback_eligibility or winback_tier. Zero qualifying orders write lifecycle_stage as NO QUALIFYING ORDERS. The resolver's LOST / DORMANT label is written as LOST. days_overdue and overdue_ratio are rounded to two decimals. There is no metrics_updated_at. purchase_consistency is 100 times (1 minus sd/mean) of tenant-timezone day intervals: Highly Consistent at 85, Consistent at 65, Variable at 40, otherwise Sporadic; fewer than two intervals is Insufficient Data. primary_order_source maps website, funnel, or store to Online Store, pos to POS, a delivery integration to Delivery Platform, manual or invoice to Manual, import to Imported, and anything else to Other. order_source_mix is source name and count. Ties for type, location, mix, and primary source use count, then spend, then the latest date. Customer type and status bands, the 30-day trend comparison, and trailing-12-month frequency labels are preserved from the resolver; those frequency labels are computed and not written. The resolver did not write qualifying_order_count, lifecycle_stage, or metrics_hash.

nodes.label: Weekly Full M06 Reconcile
nodes.rationale: On M06_FULL_RECONCILE_WEEKDAY (default Friday; invalid values use Friday) in the tenant timezone, the same daily hop ignores the 48 hour window and the 30 page cap and recomputes every distinct contact id, still with limit=100, the per-contact lock, and the metrics hash skip. Paging stops at a safety cap of 500 pages. Progress is stored on m06full:{locationId}:{YYYY-MM-DD} and continues across hops with the same time-budget cursor and waitUntil call. That cursor keeps at most 2000 contact ids, the most recently handled ones, so a large location cannot grow the Redis value without a bound. A contact that drops out of that window can be recomputed if they appear on a later page, and the metrics hash makes a repeat write a no-op. There is no second Vercel cron. The job still runs at 03:00 UTC, so a tenant whose local weekday is not the configured day yet keeps the 48 hour scan.

nodes.label: M06 Webhook Handler
nodes.rationale: POST /api/webhooks/ghl. The payload is only a signal: the handler re-fetches orders and either writes metrics or skips an unchanged hash, then returns 202. It returns 400 when locationId or contactId is missing or is not 1-64 alphanumeric characters, and 500 when processing fails so the sender can retry. Ids come from customData.locationId and customData.contactId first, then top-level locationId and contactId, then location.id and contact_id. The rest of the body is ignored and is not logged. RX Test Lab sets customData.locationId to {{location.id}} and customData.contactId to {{contact.id}} because those custom values are used first.

nodes.label: M10 Calculator
nodes.rationale: The daily cron follows the calculator's eligibility rule but diverges on inputs. The calculator read total_orders; the cron prefers qualifying_order_count and uses total_orders only when that field is empty. After M06 those two counts are the same full qualifying count. The calculator parsed last_order_date with new Date and converted to Africa/Cairo; a stored DATE is a calendar day with no tenant-timezone conversion. The calculator can emit daysOverdue; the cron does not write it. Tier None unless eligible matches the calculator. The calculator read whatever was already stored; contacts updated inside M06_RECONCILE_HOURS are recomputed first, and on the configured weekday every contact with an order is recomputed. Contacts outside the daily window still use stored fields on other days.

nodes.label: Daily M10 Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: api/cron/m10.ts. Vercel invokes GET /api/cron/m10 at 03:00 UTC (0 3 * * *). GET or POST. It lists active tenants and calls POST /api/cron/m10-tenant?locationId= once per tenant, in parallel, with the same bearer token. One tenant invocation that throws is logged and counted, and the other tenants still finish. The cron returns 200 unless every tenant invocation failed, or configuration is missing. Zero active tenants is a successful empty run.

nodes.label: M10 Win-back Eligibility
nodes.rationale: A contact is eligible when the qualifying count is at least 3, days since the last order are at least 21, the typical interval is greater than 0, and days_since_last divided by typical rounds to at least 1.5. Tier is High at 2.0 or more and Medium otherwise. Anyone else who already has order history is Not Eligible / None. Contacts with no qualifying count and no last order date are left alone. Contacts whose winback_cycle_status is In Progress are skipped. Eligibility for a contact refreshed in this hop uses the freshly computed qualifying_order_count, total_orders, last_order_date, and typical_order_interval_days, including when the hash was unchanged and the contact update was skipped. Every other contact uses stored M06 fields, with qualifying count falling back from qualifying_order_count to total_orders. Days since the last order are recomputed from last_order_date and today in the tenant timezone. The pass writes only winback_eligibility and winback_tier, and only when those values change. It does not write daysOverdue because M06 already writes days_overdue. Tier stays None unless the contact is eligible, matching the M10 calculator and not the M06 resolver, which assigned a tier from the ratio alone even when the contact was not eligible. The calculator read total_orders and whatever was already stored. The resolver computed win-back inside M06 with at least 2 orders and no 21-day minimum.

nodes.label: M10 Workflow Enrollment
nodes.rationale: M10_ENROLL_ENABLED=true adds an eligible contact to the tenant's m10_workflow_id. The flag defaults off. TENANT_M10_WORKFLOW_ID is optional until enrollment is turned on. Enrollment is recorded on m10enroll:{locationId}:{contactId} for 180 days. The eligibility fields are still written when the workflow call fails, so a failed enroll does not block the field update. A later run retries that call until it succeeds, including when the contact is already Eligible and including a later pass on the same local day. The marker is removed when the contact is not eligible, so a later cycle can enroll again. A recorded success is not repeated while the marker is present. The HTTP client does not retry the enrollment POST.

nodes.label: M10 Tenant Hop
nodes.rationale: api/cron/m10-tenant.ts runs one tenant's order reconcile, then its win-back pass, with the same bearer check. Each tenant function has its own 300 second limit so one slow location does not consume the budget of the others. The hop holds m10:{locationId}:{YYYY-MM-DD} for at least 360 seconds, longer than the function limit, and deletes that lock when the hop finishes, including when it throws. Another run the same local day is allowed once the lock is gone; field writes are unchanged when the values already match. While the lock is held, a second hop skips that tenant. Contact search is paged with searchAfter. After 240 seconds the hop stores m10cursor:{locationId}:{YYYY-MM-DD} and schedules another call with waitUntil from @vercel/functions. The next hop starts at that cursor and does not repeat the earlier page.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres
nodes.rationale: DATABASE_URL is the pooled Neon URL used for runtime reads and writes. DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED is the direct URL used only by npm run db:migrate, which applies migrations/*.sql and nothing else. The Vercel Marketplace also injects POSTGRES_URL, which this service does not read.

nodes.label: Order Detail Enrichment
nodes.rationale: The list payload does not include checkout type. After qualifying orders are filtered, the service fetches GET /payments/orders/{orderId} for the latest qualifying order. delivery.method shipping is written as Delivery and pickup as Pickup. Any other method, a missing delivery object, shipping fees, shipping rates, and payment method names are omitted. If detail says markAsTest is true, that order is excluded and the next latest is fetched, up to three detail calls. A failed detail omits last_order_type and does not fail the webhook. The detail body is not logged. The resolver set lastOrderType to null on purpose. last_order_location checks delivery.location, locationName, store, storeName, branch, then branchName, then those same names on the order. A string or an object name is accepted. Otherwise the field stays sourceName, or source.name when the flat field is absent. A missing branch and source name is written as an empty string. Test Lab details have no branch field, so the value stays the source name. favorite_item is the product name with the highest quantity, with line spend (price.amount times qty) and then the latest order date breaking ties. top_items is the first five names separated by a comma. preferred_order_type and preferred_location use the same mappings as last_order_type and last_order_location. Those four fields are written only when this pass has a cached summary for every qualifying order. An incomplete pass leaves the keys off the update so GoHighLevel keeps the previous values, and queues the contact on m06:backfill:{locationId}. The daily reconcile drains that set once summaries are complete.

nodes.label: RX Test Lab
nodes.rationale: Fixture location ekxOqjUKW7M6OV9XAVnx. fixtures/test-lab-fields.json is the final custom-field snapshot. Test-lab ids in src/schema/fields.ts are fixtures only, not ids to send for other locations. The workflow sets customData.locationId to {{location.id}} and customData.contactId to {{contact.id}}. The account only has an Order Submitted trigger. Order details have no branch field, so last_order_location stays the source name. Redacted samples: fixtures/list-orders-sample.json (amount is major units after discount, paymentStatus and liveMode present, markAsTest absent, no checkout type), fixtures/order-detail-shipping.json, fixtures/order-detail-pickup.json, fixtures/order-detail-no-delivery.json, and fixtures/contact-search-dates.json (last_order_date as YYYY-MM-DD, midnight UTC ISO, MM-DD-YYYY, and epoch milliseconds).

nodes.label: STENZ M06 Resolver
nodes.rationale: The attached M06 resolver is the starting point. Locked rules replace its qualifying filter (status completed, payment status ignored), its 0-day same-day intervals, in-M06 win-back eligibility (at least 2 orders, no 21-day minimum, tier from the ratio alone), unrounded daysOverdue, null lastOrderType, the LOST / DORMANT label, the absence of qualifying_order_count, lifecycle_stage, and metrics_hash, MM-DD-YYYY date writes, and a single limit=500 order fetch. Preserved: average interval is the mean, typical interval is the median, customer type and status bands, 30-day trend comparison, and trailing-12-month frequency labels (computed and not written). total_orders stays the qualifying count, matching the resolver.

nodes.label: TenantStore
nodes.rationale: TENANT_STORE selects the backend. neon (the default) is the multi-tenant Neon Postgres store. env is a single-tenant store for the test phase and does not need DATABASE_URL. Both decrypt the API key only in memory for the GoHighLevel call. Unknown or inactive locations do no work. API keys are AES-256-GCM ciphertext. Tests use the in-memory store. TENANT_ACTIVE=false or 0 disables a tenant; the default is active.

nodes.label: Tenant Upsert
nodes.rationale: npm run db:upsert-tenant reads the GoHighLevel private-integration token from stdin so it is not an argument. It encrypts the token with TENANT_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY, writes the ciphertext to DATABASE_URL, generates a webhook token, and stores only the SHA-256 hash. The token is printed once on stderr. stdout is upserted LOCATION_ID and does not include the token, the API key, or the ciphertext. Running the command again replaces that location's API key and webhook hash and prints a new token; the previous token stops matching. currency is stored and is not used to rescale order amounts. TENANT_ACTIVE=false stores an inactive row. Migrations must be applied first with the unpooled URL.

nodes.label: Tenants Neon Schema
nodes.rationale: migrations/001_tenants.sql is the Neon schema. npm run db:migrate applies every file in migrations/ using DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED and does not use the pooled runtime URL, so migrations do not go through the pooler.

nodes.label: Upstash Redis
nodes.rationale: REST Redis used for idempotency locks and the per-location custom-field id cache. Required when VERCEL_ENV=production under the Vercel KV names KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN. Production fails closed if that pair is missing so a memory fallback cannot silently drop dedupe in production.

nodes.label: Vercel Cron
nodes.rationale: Vercel invokes the M10 dispatcher at 03:00 UTC. There is no second cron for the weekly full reconcile; that scan is a mode of the same hop when the tenant-local weekday matches. CRON_SECRET is the bearer token Vercel Cron sends.

nodes.label: @vercel/functions waitUntil
nodes.rationale: When a tenant hop hits its time budget it schedules another call to the tenant route with waitUntil from @vercel/functions, resuming the contact-search cursor or the order-scan offset. @vercel/functions depends on @vercel/oidc, which depends on @vercel/cli-config, which depends on zod. The application itself does not import zod.

nodes.label: Webhook Token Script
nodes.rationale: node scripts/webhook-token.mjs writes the SHA-256 hash to stdout and the token to stderr once. The token is not an argument. The hash is stored on the tenant. The token is placed only in the workflow URL as ?t=. The upsert path generates a token itself; this script is for producing a pair separately.

nodes.label: Win-back Cycle Fields
nodes.rationale: The GoHighLevel workflow owns winback_cycle_status and winback_cycle_started_at. This service reads winback_cycle_status and never writes either field. Contacts already In Progress are skipped by the eligibility pass so the cron does not restart a cycle the workflow owns.

nodes.label: rxgrowth-metrics-service
nodes.rationale: Multi-tenant customer metrics for restaurant locations on GoHighLevel. A workflow Webhook action sends locationId and contactId. The service loads that tenant's API key, re-fetches the contact's orders, computes metrics, and writes them to contact custom fields. A workflow nudge recomputes M06 metrics. A daily cron writes M10 win-back eligibility from those stored fields. The README also says nothing in this repository calls GoHighLevel or provisions a Vercel project, which is ambiguous beside the described HTTP client and Vercel cron and most likely means the workflow and project are configured outside the repo.

nodes.label: Per-contact Computation Lock
nodes.rationale: A nudge with no eventId is always computed, guarded by lock:{locationId}:{contactId} for 30 seconds. If a second nudge arrives while that lock is held, it is queued on rerun:{locationId}:{contactId} (120 seconds) and the in-flight run computes once more after it finishes, so a new order a few seconds later is not dropped. The rerun flag is put back before the contact lock is released. A second nudge does not wait on the lock and returns 202 immediately. The holder computes once more after it finishes. An explicit eventId or webhookId is still deduped for 300 seconds on evt:{locationId}:{contactId}:{eventId}. A derived contact hash is not used. A trailing recompute that fails is logged as webhook.rerun_failed.

nodes.label: Runtime Custom Field Resolution
nodes.rationale: Runtime writes resolve custom-field ids with GET /locations/{locationId}/customFields?model=contact and match fieldKey, because test-lab ids are fixtures and must not be sent for other locations. The key-to-id map is cached per location in Redis for 10 minutes. A missing key or an HTTP 400 or 422 from the contact update drops that cache and loads the list once more. The mapping note cited overdue-ratio id utMAZhK2y8laZAfqAJXb; the test-lab snapshot id is PysK1ynJ47hCLa8y2G6u. Runtime mapping uses the key, and the snapshot is the id fixture. contact.customerdaysoverdue and contact.winback_status are not in the catalog and must not be referenced. npm run generate:fields regenerates src/schema/fields.ts after a fixture change.

nodes.label: Stored DATE Field Parsing
nodes.rationale: Order dates are written as YYYY-MM-DD in the tenant timezone. A stored DATE field is read as a calendar year-month-day with no tenant-timezone conversion, so a negative-offset tenant does not move the day backward. Accepted shapes are YYYY-MM-DD, legacy MM-DD-YYYY, an ISO datetime by its UTC day (including the midnight UTC string contact search returns), and epoch milliseconds. Other text such as 10/21/2026 is ignored, as are impossible dates such as 2026-02-31. 2026-10-21T00:00:00.000Z stays 2026-10-21 in America/Chicago. The STENZ resolver reformatted dates to MM-DD-YYYY. The M10 calculator parsed last_order_date with new Date and then converted to Africa/Cairo.

nodes.label: Same-day Interval Collapse
nodes.rationale: total_orders, qualifying_order_count, and lifetime value count every qualifying order, but interval math collapses orders that share a calendar day in the tenant timezone so there are no 0-day gaps. The resolver pushed a 0-day interval for same-day orders. Two orders on day 1 and one on day 11 are 3 orders and intervals [10]. Three orders on one day produce an empty interval list, empty typical_order_interval_days, and empty overdue_ratio. average_order_interval_days is the mean of the collapsed intervals and typical_order_interval_days is the median, both preserved from the resolver. qualifying_order_count is that same full count, not the count of distinct days.

nodes.label: JSON Log Redaction
nodes.rationale: Logs are JSON on stdout. The logger redacts apiKey, authorization, token, secret, bearer strings, and every query string, so webhook tokens in the URL are not written. Every contactId, contact_id, and contactIds value is replaced with the same 12-character SHA-256 prefix, so the raw contact id is never written. Do not log tenant API keys, webhook tokens, or the webhook body. Order payloads and order-detail bodies are not logged. A failed trailing recompute is logged as webhook.rerun_failed.

nodes.label: Metrics Hash Write Skip
nodes.rationale: metrics_hash is a sha256 of the formatted values this pass would write. When the stored hash matches, the contact PUT is skipped entirely, which stops a Contact Changed workflow from looping on its own write. m06_intelligence_updated_at is excluded from the hash, so the timestamp moves only when some other written value changes. last_order_type, preferred_order_type, and primary_order_source stay in the hash as an empty string when the blank value is left off the update. While a summary pass is incomplete, favorite_item, top_items, preferred_order_type, and preferred_location are left out of the hash and the update, so a second incomplete pass does not rewrite and the later complete pass is not skipped. Adding newly written keys changes the hash once for contacts that already had M06 values. An unchanged metrics hash skips the write; a second nudge is not dropped.

nodes.label: Qualifying Order Rule
nodes.rationale: Qualifying orders are liveMode and not markAsTest and amount greater than 0, with status other than cancelled, refunded, or partially_refunded, and paymentStatus in paid, unpaid, or partially_paid. Fulfillment status does not disqualify an order. markAsTest is often absent and then means not a test order. If paymentStatus or liveMode is missing, the service fetches the order detail before applying the rule. List items that already include both are used as-is. Orders whose contactId is missing or belongs to some other contact are dropped. This replaces the STENZ resolver, which required status completed and ignored payment status, so a completed refunded order qualified and an unpaid COD order qualified only when its status was exactly completed. This service does not require contactId on the order because orders are already fetched for one contact.

nodes.label: Constant-time Webhook Token Check
nodes.rationale: There is no shared webhook secret because a GoHighLevel Webhook action cannot set headers, so each location's workflow URL carries that tenant's token as the t query parameter. The store keeps only the SHA-256 hex digest (webhook_token_hash / webhookTokenHash). The token is compared with a constant-time hash check, including a stand-in hash when the location is unknown, so the response does not reveal whether that tenant exists. An unknown location, an inactive tenant, a missing hash, and a mismatched token all return the same 401 body and do no work. A tenant with no hash is rejected in every environment, including Preview and local runs. Query strings are stripped from logs. Rotate by replacing the hash; the previous token stops matching as soon as the hash is saved.

nodes.label: Zod 4.6.7 Override
nodes.rationale: The application does not import zod. @vercel/functions depends on @vercel/oidc, which depends on @vercel/cli-config, which depends on zod. That transitive copy resolved to 4.1.11, which is below the patched 4.6.7 release. package.json overrides zod to 4.6.7 so npm audit stays clean.
